label: Access location itself
summary: A function on a selectable task location that, going by its name, hands back the location entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type, and nothing in the game's interface files shows where selectable task locations appear. PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Location name
summary: Going by its name, the name of a location that can be picked for a task.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. GetName is very common after other types (traits, activity types), and those lines are only a hint.

label: Is selected
summary: Going by its name, whether this task location is the one currently picked.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Other types' IsSelected (save game items, outliner units) set the pressed look of a button; that is only a hint.

label: Click location
summary: Going by its name, the action run when the player clicks this task location.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type, so what the click does is not documented. Other types' OnClick are written as a button's onclick; that is only a hint. It returns nothing.

label: Location itself
summary: A function on a selectable task location that, going by its name, hands back the location itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types (for example Character.Self passed as an argument); those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access entry itself
summary: A function on an entry of the rally point window's selection row that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Rally point
summary: The rally point that this selected entry stands for.
details: The entries come from RallyPointWindow.GetSelectedRallyPointItems, a row shown when more than one rally point is selected. Vanilla tints each entry's banner icon with the rally point's colour (GetRallyPoint.GetColor). The game documents no return type.

label: Entry tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of a rally point entry in the rally point window's selection row.
details: Vanilla shows it when the player hovers over an entry in the row of selected rally points.

label: Is raised
summary: Going by its name, whether the troops of this selected rally point are raised.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Regiment.IsRaised in the men-at-arms window is a different type and only a hint.

label: Is shown
summary: Going by its name and use, whether this selected rally point is the one the window currently shows.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a glow behind the entry's banner and to draw the banner button as pressed.

label: Click entry
summary: The action run when the player clicks a rally point's banner in the selection row.
details: Vanilla puts it on the banner icon's onclick. What the click changes is not documented. It returns nothing.

label: Entry itself
summary: A function on an entry of the rally point window's selection row that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access unit entry itself
summary: A function on an entry of the army window's list of selected units that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Army
summary: The army that this entry of the selected units list stands for.
details: The entries come from ArmyWindow.GetSelectedUnitItems, shown when more than one army is selected. Vanilla shows the army's soldier count on the entry and a marker icon when the army is embarked.

label: Unit entry tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of an entry in the army window's list of selected units.
details: Vanilla shows it when the player hovers over one of the selected armies.

label: Is fleet
summary: Going by its name, whether this selected unit is a fleet rather than an army on land.
details: Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Is gathering
summary: Going by its name, whether this selected army is still gathering.
details: Vanilla shows an extra icon on the entry when it is true.

label: Is raised army
summary: Going by its name, whether this selected unit is a raised army.
details: Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Is shown
summary: Going by its name and use, whether this selected army is the one the army window currently shows.
details: Vanilla draws the entry's button as pressed when it is true, and shows the embarked and gathering markers only for that entry.

label: Click unit entry
summary: The action run when the player clicks an entry in the army window's list of selected units.
details: Vanilla runs it on a click and also at the end of an animation (on_finish). What it changes is not documented. It returns nothing.

label: Right-click unit entry
summary: The action run when the player right-clicks an entry in the army window's list of selected units.
details: Vanilla puts it on each entry's onrightclick. What it changes is not documented. It returns nothing.

label: Unit entry itself
summary: A function on an entry of the army window's list of selected units that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access history itself
summary: A function on the engine's selection history that, going by its name, hands back the history itself.
details: The type belongs to the engine's own interface code. Vanilla never names it; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Has next
summary: Going by its name, whether the selection history has a later entry to go forward to.
details: Part of the engine's own interface code. Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Has previous
summary: Going by its name, whether the selection history has an earlier entry to go back to.
details: Part of the engine's own interface code. Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: History itself
summary: A function on the engine's selection history that, going by its name, hands back the history itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access line itself
summary: A function on an engine selection line that, going by its name, hands back the line itself.
details: The type belongs to the engine's own interface code. Vanilla never names it; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Line colour
summary: Going by its name, the colour of the selection line, as four numbers.
details: The return type is a group of four numbers (CVector4f), the usual form of a colour with transparency. Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Line start
summary: Going by its name, the point where the selection line starts, as two numbers.
details: The return type is a pair of numbers (CVector2f). Vanilla never names it on this type; the lines found are ordinary English text that starts with the word "From".

label: Line position
summary: Going by its name, the position of the selection line, as two numbers.
details: The return type is a pair of numbers (CVector2f). Vanilla never names it on this type; the lines found only contain the English word "Position".

label: Line itself
summary: A function on an engine selection line that, going by its name, hands back the line itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Line size
summary: Going by its name, the size of the selection line, as two numbers.
details: The return type is a pair of numbers (CVector2f). Vanilla never names it on this type; the lines found only contain the English word "Size".

label: Line end
summary: Going by its name, the point where the selection line ends, as two numbers.
details: The return type is a pair of numbers (CVector2f). Vanilla never names it on this type; the lines found are ordinary English text that contains the word "To".

label: Access server info itself
summary: A function on a multiplayer server's information that, going by its name, hands back the information itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Multiplayer mode
summary: Going by its name, a text naming the multiplayer mode of the server.
details: Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Server ID
summary: The ID of the multiplayer server, which players send to invite others.
details: Vanilla shows it in the invite text: "Invite more players by sending them the Server ID:", read through GetServerInfo.

label: Server name
summary: The name of the multiplayer server.
details: Vanilla's multiplayer lobby shows it as text, read as LobbyView.GetServerInfo.GetServerName.

label: Has server ID
summary: Whether the multiplayer server has an ID.
details: Vanilla's multiplayer lobby shows or hides a part by it, read through LobbyView.GetServerInfo.

label: Has server name
summary: Going by its name, whether the multiplayer server has a name.
details: Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Is invite only
summary: Whether the multiplayer server is joined by invitation.
details: Vanilla's multiplayer lobby shows it as a check box and shows or hides parts by it, some only for the host, read through LobbyView.GetServerInfo.

label: Is public
summary: Whether the multiplayer server is public.
details: Vanilla's multiplayer lobby shows it as a check box, read through LobbyView.GetServerInfo.

label: Is single player
summary: Going by its name, whether the game behind this server information is a single player game.
details: Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Server info itself
summary: A function on a multiplayer server's information that, going by its name, hands back the information itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access category itself
summary: A function on a category of the game's settings menu that, going by its name, hands back the category itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Settings in order
summary: Going by its name, the settings of this settings menu category in their display order.
details: Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents no return type.

label: Category name
summary: The name of a category in the game's settings menu.
details: Vanilla shows it as the label of a category's group of settings in the settings menu.

label: Category itself
summary: A function on a category of the game's settings menu that, going by its name, hands back the category itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Setting categories
summary: Going by its name, the categories of settings on this settings menu page.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. The music player uses MusicPlayer.AccessCategories as a list of entries; that is another type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access page itself
summary: A function on a page of the game's settings menu that, going by its name, hands back the page itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Page name
summary: The name of a page in the game's settings menu.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of the page's button and as its tooltip.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this settings menu page is the one currently selected.
details: Vanilla draws the page's button as pressed and picks a different button frame while it is true.

label: Click page
summary: The action run when the player clicks a page's button in the settings menu.
details: Vanilla puts it on the page buttons' onclick. What exactly it does is not documented; going by the IsSelected use beside it, the page becomes the selected one. It returns nothing.

label: Page itself
summary: A function on a page of the game's settings menu that, going by its name, hands back the page itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access siege itself
summary: A function on a siege that, going by its name, hands back the siege itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Assault casualties
summary: The casualties (soldiers lost) that an ongoing assault on the fort causes each day.
details: Vanilla shows it in the "Assault in progress" tooltip of the siege window, beside the siege progress the assault adds each day. The game text does not say whose soldiers are lost.

label: Assault progress
summary: The siege progress an ongoing assault adds each day.
details: Siege progress is what the besiegers must fill up to take the holding. Vanilla shows this number in the "Assault in progress" tooltip, together with the daily casualties the assault costs.

label: Can assault
summary: Whether the player can use the button to assault the fort.
details: The siege window enables the "Assault Fort" button by it, and the siege icon on the map shows an assault marker while it is true. The game's texts say the walls must be breached before an assault can start. The game documents no return type.

label: Fort level slows siege
summary: Going by its name and use, whether the fort level (how strong the holding's defences are) is holding the siege back.
details: Vanilla shows a high-holding-level marker on the map's siege icon while it is true. The siege window's texts warn that a fort level that is too high calls for better siege men-at-arms; those texts are not tied to this function directly.

label: Assault button tooltip
summary: The tooltip of the siege window's button that starts or stops an assault on the fort.
details: The game documents no return type; vanilla uses it directly as the button's tooltip.

label: Besieging soldiers
summary: The number of soldiers in the besieging army.
details: The siege window's troop tooltip shows it as the besieging army's size, next to the garrison's. The siege only progresses while the besiegers have more soldiers than the garrison. Raid and BarterMission have their own GetAttackerMen.

label: Why siege is stuck
summary: A text explaining why the siege is not progressing.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of the pause banner that covers the siege window while the siege is blocked. The game's texts name reasons such as a besieging army smaller than the garrison, or besiegers that are moving or in battle.

label: Why stuck, short
summary: A short text saying why the siege is not progressing.
details: Vanilla writes it on the pause banner of the siege window while the siege is blocked; the full reason is in that banner's tooltip (GetBlockedReason).

label: Commander
summary: Going by its name, a commander in the siege; the game does not say on which side.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Army.GetCommander in the outliner is another type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Garrison soldiers
summary: The number of soldiers in the besieged holding's garrison (the troops defending it).
details: Vanilla shows it in the siege window. Its tooltip says the besiegers need more soldiers than the garrison for the siege to progress.

label: Siege ID
summary: The ID number of the siege.
details: Vanilla passes it to DefaultOnSiegeClick when the player clicks a siege on the map, in the outliner or in the county view.

label: Siege name
summary: The name of the siege.
details: Vanilla shows it as the title of the siege window, reached through SiegeWindow.GetSiege.

label: Siege event timer
summary: Going by its use, how far the siege has come toward its next siege event, from 0 to 1.
details: Siege events (breach, starvation, disease, desertion and so on) happen at regular times during a siege. Vanilla fills a progress circle from 0 to 1 with it beside the "Siege Event" label. The game documents no return type.

label: Siege progress
summary: The progress of the siege, which the besiegers must fill up to take the holding.
details: Vanilla shows it as the small bar on the siege icon on the map. The game documents no return type.

label: Besieged province
summary: The province whose holding is under siege.
details: The siege window shows its details through it, such as its terrain, its illustration and its fort level. Its loot goes to the besieging realm when the siege finishes. The game documents no return type.

label: Siege description
summary: A text describing the siege, shown as a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of the siege icon on the map, in the county view and in the siege window's header. The game documents no return type.

label: Troop balance
summary: Going by its name and use, the balance of soldiers between the besiegers and the garrison, as a share of 100.
details: Vanilla uses it to split the siege window's troop bar into the besiegers' part and the defenders' part. The game documents no return type.

label: Besieging ruler
summary: The ruler of the realm that is besieging the holding.
details: The siege window, through SiegeWindow.GetSiege, shows this ruler's coat of arms with a tooltip naming the besieger's primary title. The game documents no return type.

label: Has besieging realm
summary: Whether a realm is besieging the holding.
details: The siege window, through SiegeWindow.GetSiege, shows the besieger's coat of arms only while this is true.

label: Is assaulting
summary: Whether an assault on the fort is under way.
details: Vanilla labels the siege window's button "Stop Assault" while it is true and "Assault Fort" otherwise, and shows an "Assaulting!" or "Assaulted!" banner.

label: Is blocked
summary: Whether the siege is currently not progressing.
details: Vanilla shows a blocked marker on the map's siege icon and a pause banner over the siege window while it is true. The game's texts give reasons such as a besieging army smaller than the garrison, or besiegers that are moving or in battle.

label: Blocked by garrison
summary: Going by its name, whether the siege is stuck because the garrison is too large for the besiegers.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game's texts say a siege does not progress while the besieging army is smaller than the garrison; that text is not tied to this function.

label: Player is besieger
summary: Whether the player is on the besieging side of the siege.
details: The siege window, through SiegeWindow.GetSiege, colours its header green when true and red when false, and shows the assault button only to the besieging side.

label: Siege itself
summary: A function on a siege that, going by its name, hands back the siege itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Show assault button
summary: Whether the siege window should show the button to assault the fort.
details: Vanilla shows the button only when this is true and the player is on the besieging side. Whether the button can be pressed is a separate check (EnableAssaultButton). The game documents no return type.

label: Access window itself
summary: A function on the siege window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the siege window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the window's close button. It returns nothing.

label: Siege event picture
summary: The frame number of the illustration for a past siege event, picked by its place in the history.
details: Vanilla asks for entry '0' and uses the number to choose a picture from the siege events sheet, shown under the latest event's text. That entry '0' is the most recent event is inferred from this use.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Which entry of the siege event history; vanilla passes '0'.
fields.values: a number in quotes, such as '0'

label: Siege event text
summary: The text describing a past siege event, picked by its place in the history.
details: Vanilla asks for entry '0' and shows the text below the siege event timer. The game's texts show such an event as its name followed by its effect.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Which entry of the siege event history; vanilla passes '0'.
fields.values: a number in quotes, such as '0'

label: Besieger unit entry
summary: Going by its name, the unit entry for the besieging side, used by the siege window's troop row.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data of the row that shows the allied and hostile unit icons and the troop bar. The game documents no return type.

label: Wall state icon
summary: Going by its name and use, a number for the state of the besieged holding's walls, used to pick an icon.
details: Vanilla uses it as an icon frame and checks it against 1, 2 and 3 to show matching effects. The game's texts name the wall states Intact, Small Breach and Large Breach; which number is which is not stated.

label: Wall state tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about the state of the besieged holding's walls.
details: Vanilla shows it on the walls icon of the siege window, and the walls text puts the siege weapon description below it.

label: Daily siege progress
summary: How much siege progress the besiegers gain each day.
details: Vanilla shows it as "… /day" in the siege window, and shows stronger visual effects as it passes 0, 1.5, 3 and 5.

label: Daily progress tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about the siege's daily progress.
details: Vanilla shows it on the daily progress part of the siege window. The game's texts break daily progress into parts such as base, men-at-arms, besieging soldiers, assault, disease and fort level.

label: Disease state icon
summary: Going by its name and use, a number for how far disease has spread in the siege, used to pick an icon.
details: Vanilla uses it as an icon frame and checks it against 1, 2 and 3 to show matching effects. The game's texts name the states No Diseases, Sickness Spreading and Rampant Disease; which number is which is not stated.

label: Disease state tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about disease in the siege.
details: Vanilla shows it on the disease icon of the siege window.

label: Fort level tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about how the besieged holding's fort level affects the siege.
details: Fort level is how strong the holding's defences are. Vanilla shows it on the fort level part of the siege window.

label: Troop count tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about the number of soldiers on both sides of the siege.
details: Vanilla shows it on the siege window's troop row, which holds the unit icons and the bar comparing besiegers and garrison.

label: Event timer frame
summary: Going by its use, the frame number of the progress circle that counts down to the next siege event.
details: Vanilla uses it as the frame of that circle, whose fill comes from Siege.GetPhaseProgress. What the different frames mean is not documented.

label: Siege
summary: The siege shown in the siege window.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data of most of the window and reads the siege's name, its province, whether it is blocked and which side the player is on through it. The game documents no return type.

label: Siege weapon count
summary: Going by its name, the number of siege weapons the besiegers bring.
details: Vanilla shows it as a number in the siege weapons part of the window. Siege weapons are needed to breach the walls.

label: Siege weapon regiment
summary: The list of the besiegers' siege weapon regiments.
details: Vanilla lists them in the siege window and shows a different part instead when the list is empty. The game documents no return type.

label: Time to siege event
summary: Going by its name and use, a text for the time left in the current siege phase, before the next siege event.
details: Vanilla writes it in large letters below the "Siege Event" label, next to the event timer circle.

label: Siege event tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about the siege's current phase and its next siege event.
details: Vanilla shows it on the siege event part of the window. The game's texts there tell when the next siege event comes and how often they occur.

label: Siege progress tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about the siege's progress.
details: Vanilla shows it on the siege window's progress bar.

label: Siege weapon text
summary: A text about the besiegers' siege weapons.
details: Vanilla shows it in the walls tooltip, below the wall state text. The game's texts say siege weapons, or stronger ones, are needed to breach the walls.

label: Supply state icon
summary: Going by its name and use, a number for how far the besieged holding is starving, used to pick an icon.
details: Vanilla uses it as an icon frame and checks it against 1, 2 and 3 to show matching effects. The game's texts name the supply states Fully Stocked, Running Low and Starvation; which number is which is not stated.

label: Supply state tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about the besieged holding's supplies.
details: Vanilla shows it on the starvation icon of the siege window.

label: Strongest siege regiment
summary: Going by its name, the besiegers' strongest siege weapon regiment.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data of the siege weapons part of the window. The game documents no return type.

label: Time left
summary: A text for the longest time the siege can still take.
details: Vanilla shows it in the "Max Time Left" tooltip. The game's texts add that siege events can end the siege sooner.

label: Time left, short
summary: A short text for the longest time the siege can still take.
details: Vanilla shows it in the siege window while the siege is not blocked, with the "Max Time Left" tooltip that holds the longer form (GetTimeLeft).

label: Has siege event
summary: Whether the siege has a past siege event at the given place in its history.
details: Vanilla asks for entry '0' and shows the latest event's picture only when it is true.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Which entry of the siege event history; vanilla passes '0'.
fields.values: a number in quotes, such as '0'

label: Player has armies here
summary: Whether the player has armies taking part in this siege.
details: Vanilla shows the button that selects all the player's besieging armies only while it is true.

label: Select besieging armies
summary: Selects all the player's armies that are besieging this holding.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button in the siege window whose tooltip reads "Select all your besieging armies". It returns nothing.

label: Select holding
summary: Selects the holding that is under siege.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button in the siege window whose tooltip reads "Select the holding". It returns nothing.

label: Window itself
summary: A function on the siege window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Start or stop assault
summary: Starts an assault on the fort, or stops the one under way.
details: Vanilla runs it from the siege window's "Assault Fort" / "Stop Assault" button. An assault adds siege progress and causes casualties every day. It returns nothing.

label: Access icon itself
summary: A function on a Silk Road map icon that, going by its name, hands back the icon itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Bazaar building
summary: The bazaar (Silk Road marketplace) building shown on this Silk Road map icon.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data of the marketplace button on the sub-region's map icon, with a bazaar building tooltip. The game documents no return type.

label: Innovation
summary: The innovation shown on this Silk Road map icon.
details: Vanilla shows the innovation's icon with its tooltip on a paper background on the map. The game documents no return type.

label: Sub-region
summary: The Silk Road sub-region (one part of the situation's area) this map icon stands for.
details: Clicking the icon opens the sub-region window for it. The game documents no return type.

label: Has innovation
summary: Whether this Silk Road map icon has an innovation to show.
details: Vanilla shows the innovation marker on the map only while it is true.

label: Has sub-region
summary: Whether this Silk Road map icon belongs to a sub-region.
details: Vanilla shows the sub-region's map button only while it is true.

label: Icon itself
summary: A function on a Silk Road map icon that, going by its name, hands back the icon itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Should show
summary: Going by its name, whether this Silk Road map icon should be shown.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. FeedMessageItem.ShouldShow in the notifications is another type and only a hint.

label: Participant list
summary: The list of characters taking part in the Silk Road situation, as shown in the Silk Road window.
details: Vanilla shows the list for the chosen sub-region and closes it with AccessParticipantCharacterList.Close.

label: Access window itself
summary: A function on the Silk Road window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the Silk Road window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the window's close button. It returns nothing.

label: Close catalyst panel
summary: Closes the catalyst panel of the given sub-region in the Silk Road window.
details: Catalysts are happenings that add progress toward a sub-region's phases. Vanilla runs it when the player opens the participant groups instead, and from the panel's close button. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The sub-region whose catalyst panel to close.
fields.values: a situation sub-region, such as SituationSubRegion.Self

label: Catalyst
summary: The catalysts that lead toward the given future phase, listed in the Silk Road window.
details: Catalysts are happenings that add progress toward a phase of a sub-region. Vanilla lists them as entries for the phase passed in. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The future phase whose catalysts to list.
fields.values: a future situation phase, such as FutureSituationPhase.Self

label: Phase progress bar
summary: Going by its name and use, the data for the progress bar that shows how the given sub-region moves toward its phases.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data of a part of each sub-region's entry in the Silk Road window. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The sub-region the bar is for.
fields.values: a situation sub-region, such as SituationSubRegion.Self

label: Selected sub-region
summary: The sub-region currently selected in the Silk Road window.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data of the window's detail parts. A click on a sub-region's buttons selects it (SetSelectedSubRegion).

label: Situation
summary: The Silk Road situation that the window shows.
details: A situation is a long-running, region-wide state of the game, split into sub-regions with phases. Vanilla reads the situation's phases through it, for example GetSituation.GetType.GetPhases.

label: Is bad phase
summary: Whether the given sub-region is in a bad phase of the Silk Road situation.
details: Vanilla shows the bad-phase progress circle for the sub-region when it is true, and a neutral look when neither this nor IsGoodPhase is true.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a situation sub-region, such as SituationSubRegion.Self

label: Sub-region toggled
summary: Going by its name and use, whether the given sub-region's catalyst panel is open in the Silk Road window.
details: Vanilla shows the panel and draws its button as pressed when this is true and the participant list is not open.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a situation sub-region, such as SituationSubRegion.Self

label: Is good phase
summary: Whether the given sub-region is in a good phase of the Silk Road situation.
details: Vanilla shows the good-phase progress circle for the sub-region when it is true, and a neutral look when neither this nor IsBadPhase is true.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a situation sub-region, such as SituationSubRegion.Self

label: Sub-region expanded
summary: Going by its name, whether the given sub-region's entry is unfolded in the Silk Road window.
details: It takes one argument, presumably the sub-region. Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Going by the name, the sub-region to check.

label: Click decision
summary: The action run when the player clicks a decision's button in the Silk Road window.
details: Vanilla uses it on the "visit bazaar" button, which belongs to the decision visit_silk_road_market_decision and is shown only when the player may see that decision. What the click does is not documented. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The decision the button belongs to.

label: Window itself
summary: A function on the Silk Road window that, going by its name, hands back the window itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Select sub-region
summary: Makes the given sub-region the selected one in the Silk Road window.
details: Vanilla runs it together with opening the sub-region's catalysts or participant groups. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a situation sub-region, such as SituationSubRegion.Self

label: Fold sub-region
summary: Going by its name and use, unfolds or folds the given sub-region's entry in the Silk Road window.
details: Vanilla runs it together with the fold-out toggle of the sub-region's entry button. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The sub-region to fold or unfold.
fields.values: a situation sub-region, such as SituationSubRegion.Self

label: Toggle catalysts
summary: Opens or closes the catalyst panel of the given sub-region in the Silk Road window.
details: Catalysts are happenings that add progress toward a sub-region's phases. Vanilla runs it with selecting the sub-region and closing the participant list. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The sub-region whose catalysts to show or hide.
fields.values: a situation sub-region, such as SituationSubRegion.Self

label: Toggle participants
summary: Opens or closes the list of participant groups for the given sub-region in the Silk Road window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the "view participant groups" button, together with selecting the sub-region and closing its catalyst panel. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The sub-region whose participants to show or hide.
fields.values: a situation sub-region, such as SituationSubRegion.Self

label: Access situation itself
summary: A function on a situation that, going by its name, hands back the situation itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Catalyst history
summary: Going by its name, the record of catalysts that have happened in the situation.
details: Catalysts are happenings that add progress toward a sub-region's phases. Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents no return type.

label: Custom text
summary: Going by its name, the text of a custom localization run on the situation.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Other types' Custom take the key of a custom localization (a text that script picks by conditions), such as Character.Custom('…'); that is only a hint.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Going by other types' use, the key of the custom localization.

label: Center province
summary: Going by its name, the province at the centre of the situation.
details: Vanilla's natural disaster window uses it for a button that jumps to that province, shown only when the province exists. The game documents no return type.

label: Character's phase
summary: The phase of the situation that applies to the given character right now.
details: Vanilla's migration window reads the phase's type from it for a character. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose phase to look up.

label: Description
summary: The description text of the situation.
details: Vanilla shows it in the situation's tooltip, next to its icon.

label: End date
summary: The date the situation ends.
details: Vanilla shows it in the situation debug window, written out as a long date. The game documents no return type.

label: Great project
summary: Going by its name and use, the great project of the situation that belongs to the given character.
details: Vanilla's natural disaster window passes the player and shows a part with that project only when one exists. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character to look up; vanilla passes the player.

label: Situation ID
summary: The ID number of the situation.
details: Vanilla passes it, with the situation's window name, to ToggleGameViewData from the situation buttons in the main interface to open or close that situation's window.

label: Icon
summary: The icon picture of the situation.
details: Vanilla shows it on the situation buttons of the main interface and in the situation's tooltip. The game documents no return type.

label: Name
summary: The name of the situation.
details: Vanilla uses it in effect texts, for example when a situation triggers a catalyst in a sub-region and adds progress toward a phase. Going by its name, GetNameNoTooltip gives the name without the hover tooltip.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the situation, going by its name without the tooltip that GetName carries.
details: Vanilla uses it in window headers, such as the Great Steppe window's title and the natural disaster participants' heading.

label: Character's group
summary: The participant group of the situation that the given character belongs to.
details: Participants of a situation are sorted into groups. Vanilla shows the group's name in texts such as "Your Group: …" for the player, and "You are in the … of …" when a situation starts.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose group to look up.
fields.values: a character, such as GetPlayer.Self or Character.Self
